The plan conflates the two forms and may be discarding a simpler alternative without having evaluated it — or alternatively, it was evaluated but the test outcome was not recorded.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that the absolute path written into git pointer files must use forward slashes (POSIX separators) regardless of OS — e.g., convert via `pathlib.Path(realpath).as_posix()` before writing, to avoid breaking git on Windows.
evidence: Plan text: 'two files embed the template's absolute path — .tickets-tracker/.git and .git/worktrees/-tickets-tracker/gitdir'
Plan text: 'The template path is realpath-resolved before substitution (macOS reports /private/tmp/...)'

Git for Windows stores paths in worktree pointer files using forward slashes regardless of the native OS path separator; a native Windows path with backslashes in these files causes git to fail to locate the worktree's git directory.
ABSENCE: the plan mentions only the macOS symlink concern; it does not address the Windows path-separator issue in the substitution step.
findings.finding: The pointer-rewrite step writes OS-native absolute paths (from os.path.realpath or equivalent) into the two git pointer files. On Windows, os.path.realpath() returns backslash-separated paths (e.g., C:\Users\runner\...\copy\.tickets-tracker\.git). Git for Windows expects POSIX-style forward-slash paths in worktree pointer files; a backslash path written into .tickets-tracker/.git or .git/worktrees/-tickets-tracker/gitdir will not be resolved by git, silently breaking every git operation on the copied worktree.
findings.location: Approach section: 'rewrites the two pointer files explicitly' / AC: 'The template path is realpath-resolved before substitution'
scenarios: Windows platform (Git for Windows): after copytree + pointer rewrite using os.path.realpath(), .tickets-tracker/.git contains 'gitdir: C:\runner\...\copy\.git\worktrees\-tickets-tracker' with backslashes. Running `git -C copy/.tickets-tracker rev-parse --git-common-dir` fails or returns an unexpected path, causing the guard assertion in the fixture to fire and every rebar_repo-dependent test to error out on Windows CI.
findings.suggested_fix: When writing the two pointer files, convert the realpath to a POSIX path string: `path_str = pathlib.Path(os.path.realpath(copy_dir)).as_posix()`. Git on all platforms (including Git for Windows) correctly resolves forward-slash absolute paths in worktree pointer files.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify `symlinks=True` explicitly in the `shutil.copytree` call inside `_clone_template` so git-internal symlinks are preserved as symlinks rather than dereferenced into regular files.
evidence: Plan says 'add a session-scoped template fixture and a `_clone_template` helper' but gives no argument specification for `shutil.copytree`.
Python docs: `shutil.copytree(src, dst, symlinks=False, ...)` — default dereferences symlinks.
Git can create internal symlinks: e.g. alternates, and historically HEAD on some platforms.
The plan's exhaustive scan assertion ('no size limit, binaries included') covers CONTENT but not the filesystem-level symlink structure of the `.git/` directory tree.
findings.finding: The plan instructs `shutil.copytree` be used to copy the template but never specifies the `symlinks=` argument. CPython's default is `symlinks=False`, which dereferences symlinks found inside the copied tree. On some git versions and platforms, `.git/` subdirectories may contain internal symlinks (e.g., `.git/objects/info/alternates`, or `HEAD` on repos that use the legacy symref format). More concretely, if any future git version or macOS system git creates a symlink under the template's `.git/` or `.tickets-tracker/` trees, `copytree` with `symlinks=False` would silently dereference it into a regular file at the wrong inode, potentially producing a corrupt copy that passes the two-file pointer assertion but fails at runtime. The plan should explicitly specify `symlinks=True` for `_clone_template` so that git-internal symlinks are preserved as symlinks rather than being flattened.
findings.location: Scope section / `_clone_template` helper description; AC line 'The template path is realpath-resolved before substitution'
scenarios: A git version that uses a symlinked `HEAD` or `packed-refs` under `.git/` causes `copytree` to create a regular file instead of a symlink, producing a corrupt working copy that passes the pointer assertion but fails git operations at runtime.
Future macOS system git changes symlink behavior inside `.git/objects/info/`, silently breaking the copy for all 589 consumers with an opaque git error rather than a clear fixture failure.
findings.suggested_fix: In `_clone_template`, call `shutil.copytree(template, dest, symlinks=True)` to preserve any git-internal symlink structure, then overwrite the two pointer files as planned.
